Garching / Full-time / Permanent employee YOUR RESPONSIBILITIES

The What:

Keep our production running.

You make sure our machines don’t stop. In a fast-scaling production environment, you take ownership of maintenance, reliability, and quick problem solving — keeping our operations stable while we grow.

The Why:

To end COPV failure in spaceflight. The benchmark for performance, reliability, and cost efficiency. Our logistics determine whether materials are in the right place at the right time. Without flow, there is no production. Without precision, there is no reliability. Without structure, there is no scaling. Logistics is the pacemaker and heart of the mission.

Your tasks in detail and priorities:

- Maintain critical systems: Perform regular maintenance on our machines and ensure operational readiness
- Own machine reliability: Identify weak points early and prevent failures before they happen
- Support new equipment: Assist in selecting, installing, and ramping up new machines
- Document what matters: Keep maintenance, changes, and actions clearly and reliably documented
- Fix issues hands-on: Analyze faults systematically and resolve them directly on the shopfloor
- Work across boundaries: Collaborate closely with production, engineering, and external partners
- Build structure in growth: Help bring order, standards, and reliability to a rapidly growing machine park

YOUR PROFILE

- Solid technical background: Training as a mechatronics technician, industrial mechanic, electrician, or similar
- Hands-on experience: Experience in maintenance of industrial machines and equipment
- Technical versatility: Ideally familiar with machines such as CNC (milling/turning), presses, robots/cobots, or HVAC systems
- Structured working style: You work cleanly, stay organized, and document your work properly
- Problem-solving mindset: You go to the root cause and fix issues sustainably
- Hands-on mentality: You step in where needed — even beyond your core area
- Communication skills: Comfortable working with internal teams and external service providers
- Language skills: German required (at least B2), English at working level (at least B1)

WHAT WE OFFER

- High level of autonomy & real impact: Be part of shaping our high-tech production landscape
- Flexible working hours & remote work options based on mutual agreement
- Startup mindset meets aerospace innovation: Flat hierarchies, fast decisions, and space for your ideas
- Choose your own benefit: Germany ticket, Egym Wellpass, or a tax-free Give Card
- Healthy & social lunch culture: Enjoy fresh meals during shared lunch breaks
- Stunning views: Wind down on our rooftop terrace with breathtaking views of the Alps in Taufkirchen or enjoy our indoor garden in Garching-Hochbrück
- Growth opportunities: Work on exciting projects and learn from inspiring people

PhD student for TIQTOC optical atomic clock experiment for Ultra-light Dark Matter

Remuneration Group E13 | Limited: 3 years | Starting date: 01.01.2027 | ID: APDO006/2026 | Deadline: open | Part-time

DESY, with more than 2900 employees at its two locations in Hamburg and Zeuthen, is one of the world's leading research centres. Its research focuses on decoding the structure and function of matter, from the smallest particles of the universe to the building blocks of life. In this way, DESY contributes to solving the major questions and urgent challenges facing science, society and industry. With its ultramodern research infrastructure, its interdisciplinary research platforms and its international networks, DESY offers a highly attractive working environment in the fields of science, technology and administration as well as for the education of highly qualified young scientists.

The Zeuthen location of DESY has a strong focus on astroparticle and particle physics (gamma-ray and neutrino astronomy, and collider particle physics). The experimental groups are accompanied by a strong theory group. DESY Zeuthen is responsible for developing and delivering detectors for astroparticle and particle physics experiments, and is actively engaged in R&D for future applications.

With the Centre for Quantum Technology and Applications (CQTA), DESY Zeuthen is taking a leading role in applying quantum technology to challenges in particle and astroparticle physics. A new search for the effects of ultralight dark matter is being constructed, using ultra-sensitive optical atomic clocks as the sensing element. The post holder will contribute to this search, developing a test setup for networked clock comparison and frequency stabilisation. The post holder will also help to develop the procedures to collect and analyse the frequency comparisons, forming the basis of fundamental physics searches for (e.g.) ultralight dark matter.

About your role:
